source_excerpts.text:
## 1. The chosen capability

The question I selected is:

> **Can a researcher learn and choose the intervention rate of a fixed sensor-feedback program, with a finite guarantee over its entire response curve, while leaving the physical system’s hidden memory unresolved?**

The concrete operation is a two-level force-command experiment. The program observes a noisy coordinate, decides when to apply the high command, and records a transition when two consecutive post-start measurements exceed a threshold. Every four-second trial has a hard limit of **1.5 seconds under the high command**.

The setting being learned is the probability of a random intervention bit. The feedback logic, threshold, measurement processing, horizon, command levels, and duration cap are fixed before acquisition.

This target has a real interface. Optical-trap experiments have applied randomly switching force commands to DNA hairpins; the published apparatus reports 1 kHz acquisition, 0.1 pN force resolution, and 1 nm position resolution. The controlled variable is the force-clamp command, with the apparatus’s dynamics between that command and the measured molecular response. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} Open control software such as SmartTrap provides a further implementation route, although I did not install or operate hardware. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

I kept the scientific meaning of the measurement precise. The acquired prediction concerns the specified **recorded transition event**. An extension threshold in a force-clamp experiment does not, by itself, establish a hidden folding state: beads and handles can move in response to the command. A claim about molecular conformation or continuous-time first passage needs additional measurement calibration.

### Why another hidden-state reconstruction was insufficient

The strongest existing approaches already extract useful models from short, noisy single-molecule records. The recent simulation-based inference work by Dingeldein and collaborators reconstructs folding models from short constant-force measurements and explicitly discusses remaining discrepancies associated with memory or position-dependent diffusion. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

source_excerpts.text:
## 2. The central construction

The useful change is to condition **the controller’s exogenous random seed**, rather than try to reconstruct or condition the hidden physical state.

Fix a causal program \(P\) that observes the sensor history and consumes at most \(H\) binary random bits. Its only tunable parameter is the coin probability \(\theta\). For deployment, draw

\[
B=(B_1,\ldots,B_H),\qquad
B_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\theta),
\]

and let the program read those bits as needed.

The entire seed can be committed before the experiment. **Unused bits remain part of the seed after success, stopping, or budget exhaustion.**

For each fixed seed \(b\), the program interacting with the apparatus defines an unknown conditional law

\[
K(dz\mid b)
\]

for the complete measured record \(z\). This law includes hidden molecular states, actuator lag, detector filtering, electronic noise, bath memory, and the causal feedback interaction.

The learner is never given \(K\). It is only a mathematical description of what the experiment does.

Let \(R=g(z)\in[0,1]\) be the prescribed measured outcome. Grouping seeds by their number of ones gives the exact identity

\[
\boxed{
p(\theta)
=
\mathbb E_\theta R
=
\sum_{n=0}^{H}
\binom Hn\theta^n(1-\theta)^{H-n}q_n .
}
\]

Here

\[
q_n
=
\mathbb E\!\left[
R
\;\middle|\;
\text{a uniformly chosen \(H\)-bit seed containing exactly \(n\) ones}
\right].
\]

**Each \(q_n\) is the mean of an executable experiment.** Choose a uniform \(n\)-subset of the \(H\) bit positions, supply that seed to the same controller, and measure the outcome.

### Why feedback does not break the identity

The commands can depend on earlier noisy measurements. That dependence is contained in \(K(\cdot\mid b)\). The distribution of a seed under the target controller is

\[
\Pr_\theta(B=b)
=
\theta^{|b|}(1-\theta)^{H-|b|},
\]

so all seeds with the same count have the same weight. Their conditional distribution is uniform and independent of \(\theta\).

This argument would generally fail if we stratified by **actual force changes**, successful pulses, or coins used before an event. Those quantities depend on the physical response. The acquisition stratum is the count in the **entire planned seed**.

## 3. Finite acquisition and conditioning

Run \(m_n\) independent experiments with exactly \(n\) planned one-bits. Let \(\widehat q_n\) be the ordinary sample mean.

Then

\[
\widehat p(\theta)
=
\sum_{n=0}^{H}b_n(\theta)\widehat q_n,
\qquad
b_n(\theta)=\binom Hn\theta^n(1-\theta)^{H-n}.
\]

The estimate is automatically a valid probability. For binary outcomes, it is also exactly the **saturated joint Bernoulli likelihood estimator**.

That equivalence matters. An equally informed likelihood method using this representation obtains the same estimator. The construction earns a finite experimental object; it does not claim to defeat likelihood fitting through a different name.

### The finite-data bound

At a fixed \(\theta\), the individual recorded outcomes have weights \(b_n(\theta)/m_n\). Hoeffding’s inequality gives

\[
\Pr\!\left(
|\widehat p(\theta)-p(\theta)|>r
\right)
\le
2\exp\!\left[-\frac{2r^2}{V(\theta)}\right],
\]

where

\[
V(\theta)=
\sum_{n=0}^{H}\frac{b_n(\theta)^2}{m_n}.
\]

This variance proxy is known from the acquisition design. It does not require a population variance, a fitted hidden model, or asymptotic standard errors.

To certify the entire interval, take \(J=M+1\) Chebyshev nodes, with \(M>H\pi/2\), and define

\[
C=\left(1-\frac{H\pi}{2M}\right)^{-1},
\]

\[
R_\delta
=
C\max_j
\sqrt{
\frac{V(\theta_j)}{2}
\log\frac{2J}{\delta}
}.
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{
\Pr\!\left[
\sup_\theta
|\widehat p(\theta)-p(\theta)|
\le R_\delta
\right]\ge1-\delta .
}
\]

The finite mesh controls the continuum because the error is a degree-\(H\) polynomial. The proof uses the standard Bernstein/Chebyshev norming argument. **The mesh points are computational evaluations, not additional laboratory experiments.** :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

For \(L\) recorded deadlines, replace \(\delta\) by \(\delta/L\). One confidence event then covers every setting and every deadline. The estimated completion-time distribution remains monotone because it is a positive mixture of empirical distributions.

### The acquisition distribution is explicit

For the desired parameter interval \(\Theta\), define

\[
s_n=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}b_n(\theta),
\qquad
Z_H=\sum_{n=0}^{H}s_n,
\qquad
m_n=
\left\lceil N_0\frac{s_n}{Z_H}\right\rceil.
\]

This gives

\[
N_{\rm trials}\le N_0+H+1,
\qquad
V(\theta)\le\frac{Z_H}{N_0}.
\]
